newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta opposition wins local election.
newsitem.headline: Malta opposition wins local election.

text.p: Malta's opposition Nationalist Party said on Sunday it had won 51 percent of votes in local elections on Saturday in a third of Malta's districts.
The ruling Malta Labour Party did not stand in the elections, arguing that political parties should not contest local elections, but it strongly backed candidates running as independents.

The Malta electoral commission, which issued results for all 21 localities where the elections were held, said turnout on average was 62 per cent, six percent down from similar elections three years ago.
The Nationalist Party, ousted from national government in October, increased its vote by seven percent to 51 percent. Vote counting ended on Sunday afternoon.

Nationalist Party leader Eddie Fenech Adami, who is leader of the opposition, said the results were confirmation of the Nationalist Party policy on local councils. The outcome, he said, was significant, coming soon after the general election.
